question: i have a startup idea and want to build a prototype, does st olaf give out money for that
expected_answer: Yes. The Piper Center's Entrepreneurial Venture Concept Grant funds testing an idea, prototype or business concept (e.g. building a prototype, focus groups, market research). Awards range from $500 to $1,500, are judged on a rolling basis (you compete only with yourself), and applications are open September 1 to March 1 or until funding runs out, via a Handshake posting. You need to be a full-time St. Olaf student; the application is a 3-5 page business concept summary plus a pitch video or audio no longer than 3 minutes, and you should expect an answer within 4-6 weeks.

question: is there some paid summer thing where you work at a law school legal clinic
expected_answer: Yes, the Svoboda Legal Scholars Summer Program: about ten weeks in the summer doing legal research or legal support in social-impact legal clinics at law schools or legal aid organizations (2026 sites included the University of Minnesota, Mitchell Hamline, St. Thomas, Wisconsin, Notre Dame, Northwestern and Legal Aid D.C.). Participants who complete it receive a $6,500 scholarship deposited to their student account, but must cover their own housing and transportation. Students apply through Handshake in late February; a faculty/staff committee picks semi-finalists and the clinics choose the students.

question: would i even qualify? im a sophomore and im here on an f-1
expected_answer: Class year is fine (the program is for sophomores/rising juniors and juniors/rising seniors), but for 2027 the program is open only to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or students in other classifications that permit off-campus employment with a valid EAD; students only in F-1 status are not eligible. Other criteria include a strong academic record, and students can do only one St. Olaf cohort internship program. Contact the Piper Center with eligibility questions.

history.content: is there some paid summer thing where you work at a law school legal clinic

Yes, the Svoboda Legal Scholars Summer Program places students in law school legal clinics for about ten weeks in the summer, with a $6,500 scholarship for those who complete it. You apply through Handshake in late February.

question: i have a virtual interview tomorrow and dont own a blazer, can i borrow one from piper
expected_answer: Yes, the Piper Center has Blazer Check Out: sign the agreement form, stop by the Piper Center to try one on for size, and check it out with a Peer Advisor or Career Coach. It is only for on-campus or virtual interviews, the reservation is within 2 hours of the interview, and blazers must be returned within two hours of check out. Fees: $10 dry cleaning if returned in poor condition, $50 late fee if not returned within 24 hours (Friday check-outs have until Monday), and $150 replacement if not returned after 3 days.

question: i did pacon my first year, is there money for an unpaid internship in politics or public policy
expected_answer: Yes. Students who completed the Public Affairs Conversation (PACON) as first-years can get one PACON Internship Grant Award for an unpaid or underpaid public affairs internship, completed by the summer after junior year (on-campus/St. Olaf-employer internships are not eligible). Recipients must register for academic internship credit, and any employer pay is subtracted from the award. The 2025-26 award levels are up to $1,200 (fall/spring, 4 weeks and 55 hours), up to $2,500 (J-Term, 4 weeks and 120 hours) and, for summer (8 weeks, 240 hours), up to $2,500 in expenses (up to $4,000 in high-cost locations) plus a $1,500 stipend; the PACON site describes awards ranging from $500 to $4,500. PACON students are also encouraged to consider the Future Leaders in Public Service Internship Program (U.S. citizens only).

question: my roommate and i want to just swap rooms with two girls down the hall, we all agree, is that fine
expected_answer: No. Any room change not facilitated and approved by Residence Life professional staff is an unapproved room change, including swapping rooms with others or moving into a vacant space even with permission. The standard fine is $500 (possibly more). Request a change through the Room Change Request Form in the Housing Portal (not available during Room Change Freeze periods); approved moves usually get about 48 hours to complete, including returning the old key.

question: im studying abroad next spring, can i leave my stuff in storage on campus
expected_answer: Possibly, through Long Term Storage, which is for students whose permanent address is 360 miles or more from Northfield and who will be away for a whole term (e.g. study abroad, student teaching). Students are limited to six items, which must be sealed and labeled; only transparent bins (max 24 x 16 x 17 inches), polyethylene totes or suitcases are allowed, not cardboard boxes, trash bags, colored bins, electronics, refrigerators, food or bikes. Submit the Long-Term Storage Request Form; graduating students and students on leave of absence are not eligible.

question: my flight from overseas lands before move in week, am i allowed to move in early
expected_answer: Possibly. Domestic or international travel is an approved early arrival reason, but you must apply and be approved first: log into the Housing Portal, choose Applications, select the Fall Early Arrival Application, and provide a copy of your flight itinerary. Other approved reasons are fall athletics, approved college programs, and extenuating circumstances reviewed case by case; don't plan the trip until approved.

question: my boyfriend wants to stay in my room this weekend and hes driving up, what do i need to do
expected_answer: Submit the Residence Life Overnight Guest Form at least 5 business days in advance; all residents of the room must approve, and guests may stay at most 3 nights in a 10-day period (and no more than 7 days in a 31-day period). Once approved, he can get an overnight visitor parking permit (11 p.m. to 7 a.m.) by calling Public Safety at 507-786-3666; an officer meets you both at the car. Overnight visitors park in the Buntrock Commons lot (Lot A), and the host is responsible for any of the guest's parking citations.

question: how much do you make working dish in stav
expected_answer: A Stav Student Dishwasher is an entry-level Non-Standard Tier 1 job, which pays $13.50/hour (an Experienced Student Dishwasher is Non-Standard Tier 2, $14.50/hour; Stav Student Supervisor is Tier 3, $15.50/hour). Food service jobs use the Non-Standard pay structure, which is higher than the Standard tiers ($12.00, $12.50 and $13.00) that cover most other campus jobs.

question: whats the max hours i can work at my campus job? can i work more over jterm
expected_answer: During fall and spring semesters students can work up to 20 hours per week (domestic and international). During the J-Term break and summer you can work up to 40 hours per week if you are not taking classes. F-1 students likewise may not exceed 20 hours a week while classes are in session, with full-time work allowed during official breaks longer than one week.

question: do i have to register my bike? does it cost anything
expected_answer: Yes. All bicycles and scooters on campus must be registered with Public Safety and display a current St. Olaf bicycle permit (there's no separate scooter permit); permits are free for students. Unregistered bikes can be impounded, and Public Safety only investigates thefts of bikes that were registered and locked. Park only in bike racks, and electric scooters are not allowed inside buildings or residence halls.

question: its late and i dont want to walk back to my dorm alone, can someone walk with me
expected_answer: Yes, request a safe walk (on-campus walking escort) by calling Public Safety at 507-786-3666 (x3666 on campus). The current About Public Safety page says the service is available any time classes are in session, but calls for service take priority so you may need to wait for an officer. Older pages give different hours (24/7 on the Safe Walk page, or 7 p.m. to 1 a.m. with student Community Service Officers on days classes are in session); giving the current any-time-in-session answer or noting the discrepancy is correct.

question: can health services give me a doctors note for missing class when i was sick
expected_answer: No. Health Services does not provide excuse notes for missed classes, labs, work, clinicals or athletic events. You are responsible for notifying your professors (and coaches or supervisors) and arranging missed work, ideally before missing class, and are encouraged to cc your class dean. Athletic restriction or clearance notes come from sports medicine.

question: is there a way to talk to a counselor for a few min without making a whole appointment
expected_answer: Yes, Let's Talk: a confidential, informal 15-20 minute drop-in consultation with a Counseling Center counselor (not formal counseling), first come first served. It runs 3-4 p.m. Mondays at the Taylor Center and Tuesday through Friday at the Counseling Center, starting the first day of the semester; it is not available during breaks or holidays.

question: is there a deadline to switch my meal plan
expected_answer: Yes. Meal plan changes can only be made until 4:00 p.m. on the 3rd business day of the term, by logging into SIS, going to the Financials tab and choosing Meal Plan from the drop-down (click Ok to save).

question: ok what if i move into a townhouse next year, can i just drop it then
expected_answer: No. As of 2026-27, all townhouse residents are enrolled on a full meal plan and are no longer eligible for the partial plan; they can pick any full plan, including the new 10 Meal Plan (same price as other full plans, fewer meals and more Flex Dollars: $405 per semester). Only students living off campus in non-St. Olaf housing may drop the meal plan entirely.

history.content: do my unused meal swipes roll over to the next week
No. Each meal plan week runs from Friday breakfast through Thursday dinner, and unused meals are forfeited at the end of the week.

question: got a parking ticket i think was a mistake, how do i fight it
expected_answer: File an appeal in Flex Port within seven days of the citation date, or you lose the right to appeal and the fine is billed; don't pay it first, because paying accepts responsibility and forfeits the appeal. Valid reasons are officer error (photos strongly suggested) or emergencies/extenuating circumstances. The Parking Advisory Committee (three staff, two students) can void it, turn it into a warning, or uphold it, and emails a decision within 14 days; its decision is final.

question: what time does tostrud close on fridays
expected_answer: The current Recreation page lists Tostrud's regular academic-year building hours as Friday 6:30 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. (Mon-Thu 6:30 a.m.-11 p.m., Sat 9 a.m.-9 p.m., Sun noon-11 p.m.), with reduced hours possible during breaks. An older Public Safety building-hours page says Skoglund/Tostrud closes at 8:45 p.m. on Fridays; giving 9 p.m. or noting the discrepancy is correct.

question: i belay at my climbing gym back home, can i just go climb at tostrud
expected_answer: Not right away. Everyone must complete the Climbing Wall Waiver (once per academic year) and check in at the desk, and all climbers must renew belay certification each academic year, even with a current certification from another facility, by passing one belay test with a qualified instructor. Climbing shoes are required (no street shoes), and the wall is only for members of the St. Olaf community.

question: how do i get to msp airport for thanksgiving break, is there a shuttle
expected_answer: Yes, Northfield Lines runs shuttles to MSP for official college breaks at $45 each way (book online; be there 5 minutes before departure). There's also a daily Northfield Lines service from Buntrock Commons to the Mall of America and MSP while St. Olaf and Carleton are in session: $42 each way Monday-Thursday, or $20 each way Friday-Sunday with St. Olaf code STO34226; tickets must be bought in advance.

question: does the campus post office take credit cards? and is it open saturday
expected_answer: No credit cards: the Post Office accepts cash, check and Ole Cards (not Flex Dollars). During the academic year it is open Saturday 10 a.m.-1 p.m. for package pick-up only (Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-4 p.m. all services, 4-5 p.m. package pick-up only; closed Sundays). It's in Buntrock Commons room 104.

question: how long can i keep a library book, and what happens if someone else wants it
expected_answer: Students can check out books, government documents and scores for 7 weeks. Anyone can place a recall on a checked-out item, which makes it due in four days; you'll be emailed, and if you don't return it promptly there's a $5.00 per day per item late fee.

question: the library doesnt have a book i need for my paper, can i get it from somewhere else
expected_answer: Yes, through Resource Sharing (formerly Interlibrary Loan) for items not owned by St. Olaf or Carleton. Search Catalyst, use 'expand your search' or the 'Still didn't find what you need?' link, and submit a Catalyst request form. Articles or chapters often arrive within a few hours and physical books within several days; track requests in your Catalyst account and email libshare@stolaf.edu with questions.

question: lost my ole card, how much is a new one
expected_answer: A replacement Ole Card costs $25, charged to your Ole Dollars account (no fee for legal name changes). Log in and click Submit on the Ole Card replacement page to disable the lost card right away, since you're responsible for transactions before it is deactivated.

question: if i tell my JC about something that happened to me sexually, do they have to report it? who can i talk to confidentially
expected_answer: Yes: college employees, including students in their work roles such as Junior Counselors, must share reports of sex discrimination, harassment or sexual misconduct with the Director of Equal Opportunity, who then offers to meet (meeting is your choice and doesn't start an investigation automatically). Confidential resources include SARN, the student advocate network (Buntrock Commons 14, 507-786-3777, sarn@stolaf.edu), the Counseling Center (New Hall 046, 507-786-3062), TimelyCare, and the college pastors and chaplains (Boe Chapel lower level, 507-786-3092).

question: does st olaf have a student health insurance plan i can sign up for
expected_answer: Not for domestic students: St. Olaf no longer offers a Student Health Insurance Plan for domestic students. There is an international student health plan; questions about it go to Student Accounts. Health Services does not manage student health insurance, and students should check with their own insurer about what's covered.

question: can i get my preferred name on moodle and my id without changing it legally
expected_answer: Yes. Email the Registrar's Office (registrar@stolaf.edu) to use a changed first name. It will appear on things like Moodle, your student ID card, St. Olaf Gmail, the online directory, class rosters, the diploma and the Commencement program, but your legal first name stays on tax documents, financial aid and billing, transcripts, paychecks, Registrar's records, study abroad documents and transfer credit evaluations.

question: need proof im enrolled for my car insurance discount, how do i get that
expected_answer: Current students can get an enrollment verification letter through SIS: Personal, then Clearinghouse Services, which opens the National Student Clearinghouse self-service site. If the recipient needs something else or a letter on college letterhead, email registrar@stolaf.edu with what the letter should say or use the Enrollment Verification Form; allow one business day.

question: i got a 5 on ap calc bc, what does that get me
expected_answer: A 4 or 5 on AP Calculus BC earns 2.00 credits, equivalent to MATH 120 and MATH 126, places you into MATH 220, and fulfills the Quantitative and Computational Reasoning OLE Core requirement; take the math placement survey to confirm placement.

question: when is the final for my tues thurs 1:20 class this semester
expected_answer: For fall 2026, classes meeting 1:20-2:45 p.m. Tuesday / 2:15-3:35 p.m. Thursday have their final exam on Tuesday, December 22, 1:00-3:00 p.m.

question: ugh thats my third exam that day. can i move one of them
expected_answer: Possibly. If you have three in-class final exams on the same day, you may request an alternative time for one of them by filling out the Petition to Move an Exam to a Different Date and Time form (Registrar's website, Forms & Requests), which goes through the instructor to the department chair or program director. Faculty are not obligated to agree, since some exam formats need everyone in the room at the same time.

history.content: when is the final for my mwf 9:05 class this fall
For fall 2026, MWF 9:05-10:00 a.m. classes have their final exam on Thursday, December 17, 9:00-11:00 a.m.

question: if i take a semester off do i have to reapply to get back in
expected_answer: Not if you take an approved leave of absence. A student in good academic standing applies to the Dean of Students Office; an approved leave lets you return without reapplying through Admissions and register and do room draw at the normal times. You must pay the minimum tuition deposit at least four weeks before registration or room draw and notify the Registrar's Office and Dean of Students Office that you're returning (medical leaves may require provider documentation). Contact the Dean of Students Office (507-786-3615, readmission@stolaf.edu) about returning.

question: a new major got added after i started here, am i allowed to declare it
expected_answer: You follow the graduation requirements in the catalog for the year you first entered St. Olaf as a degree candidate, but if you want to declare a major or concentration not available under your entering catalog year, you can request to go up in catalog year; contact the Registrar's Office.

question: roughly how much does a jterm abroad trip cost
expected_answer: January Term programs cost $720-$3,950 for U.S. programs and $3,680-$6,900 for international programs (semester/year programs average $2,000-$5,000 above the cost of studying on campus). There are no application fees, and scholarships are available for all St. Olaf study abroad/away programs.

question: do i need my own health insurance when i study abroad or does st olaf cover me
expected_answer: You need your own: all students studying abroad/away must have adequate U.S.-based health coverage if they return to the U.S. at any time during the academic year (e.g. a parent's plan or a self-arranged plan). St. Olaf program participants automatically get EIIA international travel insurance, but it is emergency, secondary coverage and does not replace comprehensive U.S.-based insurance. International students abroad the full year without returning to the U.S. are exempt from the college health insurance requirement.

question: im an international student, can i skip jterm and fly home for it
expected_answer: Possibly. F-1 students must enroll full-time in fall, Interim and spring of their first year, and every fall and spring after that. You may take an Interim vacation once you have studied full-time at St. Olaf for nine consecutive months; fill out the request form (on the Forms and Resources page), and if you'll be outside the U.S. the Visa Coordinator adds a note to your I-20 for re-entry. You still need three full-credit Interim courses to graduate.

question: what happens if my gpa drops and i lose my merit scholarship, is that money just gone
expected_answer: Merit scholarships renew automatically if you meet the renewal requirements (generally Satisfactory Academic Progress: a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher and completing at least 67% of courses), checked once a year in June. If you have demonstrated financial need, lost merit aid is replaced with other need-based aid, so you likely won't lose gift dollars. Without demonstrated need, the scholarship is lost until you meet the criteria again; if your grades improve, notify the Financial Aid Office to have it reviewed and reinstated. Fine arts scholarships go through Molly Boes Ganza (boes1@stolaf.edu).

question: im undocumented, can i still get financial aid from st olaf
expected_answer: Yes. Undocumented students can receive St. Olaf grants, scholarships, work study and loans, outside scholarships, and the Minnesota State Grant if they are Minnesota residents. Merit scholarships come through the admission application. For need-based aid you complete the CSS PROFILE (no Social Security number required; St. Olaf's code is 6638; the 2027-28 PROFILE opens October 1, 2026).

question: my laptop died and i cant afford to fix it, is there any emergency money
expected_answer: Possibly, through the Dean of Students Emergency Fund for currently enrolled students, which covers technology (laptop or tablet) repair among other unexpected expenses. For laptop requests you must have used all financial aid options, including loans, first; cell phones are never covered, and laptop requests aren't approved after spring break of senior year. Students typically get funding once per academic year, up to $1,000 (most requests are $300-$500), it doesn't need to be repaid, and denials cannot be appealed. Submit the request form; questions go to Corrie Zoltai (zoltai1@stolaf.edu).

question: whats actually in the engineering studies concentration, how many classes
expected_answer: The Engineering Studies concentration is 11-12 credits: core math (MATH 119 or 120, MATH 126, MATH 220, MATH 226 or PHYS 375, MATH 230), CHEM 125 or CHEM 122, one of the physics tracks (2-3 credits, including intro computer science in one track), plus three electives, ideally including a design course (PHYS 160 or the Engineering Design Practicum). It's meant to be paired with a major in a natural science or math to prepare for graduate work in engineering.

question: how does the 3-2 thing work, what would i major in here
expected_answer: St. Olaf has no four-year engineering bachelor's degree; the 3-2 program with Washington University in St. Louis is for physics majors: you spend three years at St. Olaf earning a physics bachelor's, then two years at Washington University for a bachelor's in engineering. A 3-3 option instead spends three years at Washington University for a master's in engineering. Both have specific transfer prerequisites.

history.content: can you major in engineering at st olaf
There's no four-year engineering major, but there is an Engineering Studies concentration and a 3-2 program with Washington University in St. Louis.

question: is it true math majors kind of design their own major? how many classes is it
expected_answer: Yes. Math majors build an Individualized Mathematics Proposal (IMaP) with a math faculty member, approved by the chair/program director; it normally totals about 10 courses: two semesters of calculus, linear algebra, and at least seven intermediate/advanced courses, including two transition courses (MATH 242, 244 or 252), intermediate courses from at least three perspectives (computation/modeling, continuous/analytic, discrete/combinatorial, axiomatic/algebraic), and at least two Level III courses, one in a designated Level II-III sequence. Up to two related statistics or computer science courses can count.

question: can i take orgo 1 in the spring? and what do i need first
expected_answer: No, CHEM 247 Organic Chemistry I is offered annually in the fall semester only. Its prerequisite is CHEM 126 (or instructor permission); CHEM 126 itself requires CHEM 125 or CHEM 122 plus concurrent or previous MATH 119 or MATH 120.

question: i want to be an elementary school teacher, can i get licensed through st olaf
expected_answer: No. St. Olaf does not offer an elementary (K-6) classroom teaching license; students interested in elementary education can take some education courses at St. Olaf but must complete licensure after graduation at another institution. St. Olaf's licenses are K-12 music, grades 5-8 general science, grades 5-12 communication arts/literature, mathematics and social studies, and grades 9-12 biology, chemistry and physics.

question: could i do my student teaching in another country
expected_answer: Yes, St. Olaf offers student teaching abroad at international schools in Mussoorie or Kodiakanal, India and Cuernavaca, Mexico, in the fall semester. Apply by October 1 one year before the placement year; you need a minimum overall and content-area GPA of 3.3 and recommendations from your content department chair(s) and the Education Department, and Mexico applicants need the Spanish language requirement or equivalent proficiency. Placements meet Minnesota licensure requirements; contact Elizabeth Leer, Director of Student Teaching Abroad.

history.content: can i get a license to teach high school chem here
Yes. St. Olaf offers a grades 9-12 chemistry teaching license; you'd complete a chemistry major plus the Education Department's licensure requirements.

question: can you get both a BA and a BM? how long does that take
expected_answer: Yes, through the B.A./B.M. double-degree option. Most students need five years (it may not be possible in five when the B.A. major is a natural science), and some need up to 43 credits; the final two years must be in residence with 17 of the last 20 credits through St. Olaf. You pick one of five B.M. majors and any B.A. major except music or music for social impact. Fifth-year students remain eligible for St. Olaf financial aid, and you get two diplomas but one graduation ceremony.

question: whats enduring questions, do i have to apply, and what gen eds does it knock out
expected_answer: Enduring Questions is a two-year, five-course humanities sequence (QUEST 113, 115, 116, 217, 218) in which first-year participants live in the same residence hall and keep the same faculty. No separate application: choose it as your top First-Year Experience choice on the Advising Questionnaire, and take the courses in sequence. It covers First-Year Seminar (QUEST 113), Religion, Faith and Values (115), Writing and Rhetoric (116), Global Histories and Societies plus Writing Across the Curriculum (217), and Creativity plus Ethical Reasoning (218).

question: does it actually matter if i visit or do an interview when applying
expected_answer: Yes, St. Olaf says it considers your engagement with Admissions (demonstrated interest) during application review. Ways to engage include visiting in person or virtually and interviewing: staff offer in-person interviews while traveling in the fall and virtual interviews scheduled through your Admissions Officer's Calendly. Interviews are approached as conversations about your academic interests, community involvement, experiences and college search.

question: coming for a campus tour with my parents, where do we park
expected_answer: Admissions visitors park in the admissions lot (Lot F), just northeast of the roundabout; if your visit was coordinated with Admissions there should be a personalized reserved space. Visitors don't pay for parking. Downtown Northfield businesses also give discounts if you show your visit name tag or email confirmation.

question: how do i walk on to the womens hockey team, whos the coach
expected_answer: Not answerable from Lefse's pages: athletics rosters, coaches and tryout information are not covered (the ice arena page only says the men's and women's hockey teams play there). Lefse should say it couldn't find this and suggest contacting St. Olaf Athletics; it must not name a coach (an old magazine article names a men's hockey coach, which is not an answer).

question: does the bookstore buy back textbooks at the end of the semester, how much do you get
expected_answer: Not answerable: the public pages say the bookstore is operated by Barnes & Noble in lower Buntrock, sells used textbooks when possible, and lists hours and items on its own website (phone 507-237-7641), but nothing about buyback or buyback rates. Lefse should say so and point to the bookstore, without inventing a percentage.

question: how much does it cost per page to print in rolvaag, do we get free printing
expected_answer: Not answerable: the public pages don't give student printing prices or a print allowance (the Print Center pages cover departmental print orders). Lefse should say it couldn't find it and suggest the IT Helpdesk, without inventing prices.

question: can i use one of my meal swipes to bring my friend from carleton into stav
expected_answer: Not answerable: meal plan pages explain weekly meals, Flex Dollars and that the Ole Card is needed for access, but say nothing about guest swipes or bringing a non-student guest. Lefse should say it couldn't find a guest swipe policy and suggest asking Bon Appetit or Student Accounts, not claim a policy either way.

question: how fast is the wifi in the dorms, like what speed
expected_answer: Not answerable: no public page states residence hall internet speeds. Lefse should say it couldn't find this and suggest the IT Helpdesk.

question: who's the easiest prof for intro psych
expected_answer: Not answerable: St. Olaf's pages don't rate professors, and Lefse should not rank or recommend instructors as 'easy'. It can suggest looking at the class schedule or talking with an advisor.

question: whats my gpa right now
expected_answer: Lefse cannot see personal records. It should say so and point the student to SIS (or their advisor/Registrar's Office) to check their GPA, without guessing.

question: did financial aid get my fafsa yet
expected_answer: Lefse cannot see personal records or application status. It should say so and suggest checking with the Financial Aid Office (finaid@stolaf.edu) or the student's aid portal, without guessing.

question: whats the derivative of sin(x)/x
expected_answer: Off-topic homework question; Lefse should politely say it only answers questions about St. Olaf and not solve it.

question: what year did the berlin wall fall
expected_answer: Off-topic trivia; Lefse should politely decline and say it answers questions about St. Olaf.
